items.title: *The Week in 15 Selections*
items.content:
Happy Monday, I’m back with links! I spent my weekend experiencing friendship and eating delicious things, which was a delight. It is so, so nice to spend time with people you care about and celebrate them. I also read a good amount, so god-willing I’ll have at least one book to recommend next week.

Already, it is getting cooler and darker and I’m dreaming about how much reading I will get done this winter. Last winter was my winter of , which I would not shut the fuck up about. Can’t wait to find out which novel will dominate my cold months this year! Will it be Russian again? Only time will tell!

I will be sending out my Top Purchases of the Year the Monday before Thanksgiving. The next week will be reader’s choices! If you bought something great and weird this year, please respond to this email so I can add it!

  1. Alex Barasch at got the only interview about YOU CAN SEE EVERYTHING that turned into a magnificent blog. It really added to my experience and understanding of the film, which truly cannot be said for most stories.

  2. my ban on buying fish objects becomes harder and harder to uphold every week. Look at this clip that reader Leah taunted me with on Instagram

  1. “In the 1960s, an eccentric behavioral psychologist named James McConnell(opens a new tab) convinced the scientific establishment that planarian worms, like Pavlov’s dogs, could be classically conditioned — and that memories of this training could be transferred from worm to worm through cannibalism. These bizarre findings were replicated by other scientists, and worm training became a staple of high school science fairs. Now, 60 years later, the worms have stopped learning, and nobody knows why.”

  1. I finally got around to reading the GQ article about having two kids and lol at this “” I respect all parents. Good luck to y’all!

  2. Usually I’m quite against Dumb Bro Cooking of rice and chicken, but I did make this chicken dump meal from a TikTok this week and frankly, it was delicious. I used twice as much lemon.

  3. This blog is way too fucking long and desperately needed an editor, but it did made me think about how writers prioritize rhythm in their writing over other, just as good, rhetorical priorities.

  4. If anyone knows anyone at Grover Rad please EMAIL ME I’m desperate to own this coat but I do not have $2000 for a statement coat, I am a mere blogger.

  1. I’m considering breaking my heart in a new and terrible way: getting into men’s basketball

  2. This is literally my dream house. It makes me want to cry looking at it. The tub! the chickens! The WALL COLOR! I bought a lottery ticket last week in the hopes I would simply win and my life could be complete by owning this house, but I did not win.
